clue.text: Wild screams about a fearful atrocity

indicators.note: wild letters run out of control, so the word screams and the a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Terrified shrieks greet news of a dreadful outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges SCREAMS plus A; 'about' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the brutal slaughter of many people, a dreadful atrocity.

indicators.note: the elk is pictured straddling the river, so its letters go round the other piece

parts.note: the European elk is the same animal North Americans call a moose
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A sullen elk wades across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose describes a sullen, gloomy temperament.

clue.text: Said to change a good man into a bad one

indicators.note: the letters of said, with the good man, are told to change their order

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is the crossword's stock good man

explanation.surface: It is claimed a virtuous man can be corrupted into a wicked one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges SAID plus ST into a cruel person.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist takes pleasure in inflicting pain, a thoroughly bad person.

definitions.meaning: if no one is on the left, everybody is on the right side
unharmed, fine, without injury

explanation.definitionFit: Read whimsically, everyone being on the right means nobody left; ordinarily the phrase means safe and unhurt.

definitions.meaning: a tear or rip in cloth
to hire out property for regular payment

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a tear in fabric and a verb for letting property out for payment.

parts.note: the clue speaks as the letter I, which in lower case carries a point above it

explanation.definitionFit: A lower-case letter i has a point placed over it, which is what being so marked means.

parts.note: in cricket a batsman given out has been dismissed
a cry is a call or appeal for something

explanation.surface: Fielders shouting for a wicket provoke a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielders appeal to the umpire for a dismissal; here 'Appeal for dismissal' is read as CRY for OUT, set in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud public protest or clamour is an uproar.

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word art reads backwards

parts.note: verse is writing in metrical lines, poetry

explanation.surface: An angry remark concerning painting and poems.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across something, to cross it.

clue.text: Catastrophe after there are changes in star side

indicators.note: changes made in the phrase star side mean its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A sports team in disarray after its leading player alters the line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes in' rearranges STARSIDE; 'after there are' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden calamity, a catastrophe.

parts.note: read as re-act, to act again, which is to redo
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means smelling strongly of something, hence odorous.

annotationWithheld.why: Takes a duck aboard (6): TEAL inside SS, but 'aboard' must both supply SS (on a steamship) and signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs.

clue.text: Massage a girl with this illness

parts.note: to massage is to rub
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A masseur treats a young woman suffering from a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella, German measles, is an infectious viral disease.

clue.text: The bird is roosting inside the hide

indicators.note: a bird roosting inside something sits within it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin

explanation.surface: A bird watcher's hide has a bird perched inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roosting inside' signals the insertion; 'the hide' looks like a birdwatchers' shelter but means an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch.

indicators.note: beating up the word squatter knocks its letters into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Quartets are groups of four, especially of musicians.

definitions.meaning: to score is to scrape or mark a surface
starting from ... means from nothing, the very start

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to mark a surface with a line, and also the starting line, as in starting from nothing.

definitions.meaning: to clot is to become dense or set
the saying that the plot does this as a story grows complicated

explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that clots becomes denser, and the stock phrase says a plot does the same as intrigue deepens.

clue.text: Not much land but of sound promise

indicators.note: sound tells us the promise is said aloud, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: I'll, as in I will, is a promise

explanation.surface: A small patch of earth, but a firm pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction I'll, a promise, is pronounced the same as the island word.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is a small island, not much land at all.

parts.note: to pen is to write
a chant is a simple song or psalm

explanation.surface: A composer's urge to compose a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or leaning towards something.

clue.text: Tag along with a riot stirred up by him

definitions.text: Tag along with a riot stirred up by him

indicators.note: stirring up mixes the letters of tag and a riot into a new order

explanation.surface: The troublemaker who whips up a riot attaches himself to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred up' rearranges TAG plus A RIOT; the whole clue also describes a rabble-rouser.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator is someone who stirs up public unrest, the very person behind a riot.

clue.text: Cockney's full set of dentures, he says, tickles the palate

indicators.note: a Cockney accent drops sounds and turns th into f, changing how the phrase comes out
he says tells us we hear the Cockney speaking, so the spelling follows his pronunciation

parts.note: a full set of false teeth, a pair of them, upper and lower

explanation.surface: A Londoner talking about his false teeth, oddly enough, whets the appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech turns 'a pair of teeth' into something like 'a-pair-i-teef'. A Cockney is a working-class Londoner, famous for th becoming f.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is a drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

definitions.meaning: sharpness or keenness, as a knife or a remark has
the rim or border of something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means incisive sharpness and also the brink or rim of something.

clue.text: Moves at speed to go around everyone, taking sec-end in parking

indicators.note: go is placed around everyone, so its letters enclose the other word

parts.note: taken as written
everyone is all
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A driver speeds round everybody and grabs the second space in the car park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container. 'sec-end' reads oddly as printed; it stands for second, abbreviated in the usual way.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse gallops when it runs at its fastest pace.

clue.text: Cutting a ring in the wood

indicators.note: the ring sits in the wood, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A woodcutter carves a circle in timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a channel cut into a surface, a cutting.

definitions.meaning: a woman who launders clothes
the small rubber ring that seals a tap

explanation.definitionFit: A laundress cleans clothes for a living, and a tap has a rubber ring inside it that stops leaks.

definitions.meaning: a brief fall of rain
a gauge displays a reading, so it is one that shows

explanation.definitionFit: A brief fall of rain is one sense; read as show-er, it is anything that shows, as a measuring dial does.

definitions.meaning: a large waterfall
clouding of the lens of the eye

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a great waterfall and also a clouding of the eye's lens that dims sight.

clue.text: Extra effort required to get out of it

definitions.text: Extra effort required to get out of it

parts.words: Extra effort required to get out of it
parts.note: hard exertion leaves you puffing, the state of being short of air

explanation.definitionFit: Strenuous exertion leaves a person panting, out of air in the lungs.

clue.text: A female one's a butter producer

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a female
one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: One woman makes her own butter.
explanation.definitionFit: The shea tree of West Africa yields a vegetable fat called shea butter.

clue.text: The case for getting something done

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit brought in court
the process of doing things

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a legal suit brought before a court, and also the doing of things, activity rather than talk.

parts.note: chats are small songbirds such as the stonechat

indicators.note: the word who is disrupted, its letters thrown into another order

explanation.definitionFit: A talk programme on TV with a host interviewing guests is a kind of broadcast performance.

definitions.meaning: J M W ..., the English landscape painter
one who turns wood or metal on a lathe

explanation.definitionFit: J M W Turner was a famous English landscape artist, and a lathe operator shapes wood by turning it.

clue.text: A route more attractive, they say, for the traveller

parts.note: a way is a route

indicators.note: they say signals a sound-alike, so more attractive is heard not seen

parts.note: fairer means prettier

explanation.surface: A traveller picks the prettier path.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIRER sounds the same as FARER, one who fares or travels.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone journeying on foot, a traveller.
